name: bedrock-vscode-chat
displayName: AWS Bedrock Provider for GitHub Copilot Chat
description: Native AWS Bedrock integration for GitHub Copilot Chat. Brings Claude, Amazon Nova, Llama, Mistral and more into your editor with streaming, function calling, and vision support across AWS regions.

languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.infere.description: Map of model IDs to inference profile ARNs or IDs. Use this to route specific models through application inference profiles. Example: { "anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6": "arn:aws:bedrock:ap-southeast-2:123456789012:application-inference-profile/abc123" }
languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.infere.title: Inference Profile Overrides

languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.manual.title: Manual Models
languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.manual.markdownDescription: Manually declared Bedrock models. Use this when the environment blocks `bedrock:ListFoundationModels` / `bedrock:ListInferenceProfiles` (e.g. a restrictive Service Control Policy) but still allows Converse/InvokeModel, or to pin an explicit set of models. If auto-discovery fails and this list is non-empty, the extension falls back to these models instead of erroring; otherwise entries are merged with discovered models.

name.description: Display name shown in the model picker. Defaults to the id.

inferenceProfile.description: Inference profile ID or ARN to invoke instead of the bare id (e.g. "global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8"). Most cross-region models require this.

vision.description: Whether the model accepts image input.

languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.maxOut.title: Max Output Tokens (0 = model maximum)
languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.maxOut.markdownDescription:
**`0` means "use the model's own maximum"**, which is the recommended setting. Any other value is a hard cap on output tokens per response.

A low cap truncates large tool calls part-way through their JSON arguments, so the model's edit fails with an invalid-arguments error. It also breaks extended thinking: reasoning tokens are paid for out of this limit, so the cap must exceed the reasoning budget plus room for an answer. With `#languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.thinking.enabled#` on, this is raised automatically when left at `0`, and a request whose explicit cap is too small for `#languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.thinking.effort#` is rejected up front with an explanation.

Raise this above the detected maximum if your model supports more than the extension discovers.

languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.prompt.title: Enable Prompt Caching
languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.prompt.markdownDescription: Insert [Bedrock prompt-cache checkpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-caching.html) around the system prompt, the tool schemas and the most recent conversation turns. Long agent sessions resend the same prefix every turn, so caching it cuts both latency and cost substantially. Applied only to models known to support it, and skipped when the conversation is too short to be cacheable. Cache reads and writes are reported in the **Bedrock Chat** output channel.

languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.thinki.title: Enable Extended Thinking
languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.thinki.markdownDescription:
Ask models that support extended thinking to reason before answering. Ignored by models without a reasoning mode. While active, `temperature` and `top_p` are omitted and a forced tool choice is relaxed to automatic, because the models reject those combinations.

Reasoning tokens are spent out of `#languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.maxOutputTokens#`, so that limit must cover the reasoning budget **and** the visible answer. Leaving it at `0` (the default) always works; an explicit cap that is too small for the chosen effort is reported before the request is sent.

languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.thinki.title: Thinking Effort
enumDescriptions: Least reasoning, lowest latency and cost.
Maximum reasoning. Slowest and most expensive.
languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.thinki.markdownDescription:
How much reasoning to request. Newer models take this directly and choose their own token budget; older ones convert it into a budget, which `#languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.thinking.budgetTokens#` can override.

Higher levels need a correspondingly higher `#languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.maxOutputTokens#`, because reasoning tokens come out of that limit: about 6k for `low`, 12k for `medium`, 20k for `high` and 37k for `xhigh`. Leave that setting at `0` and this is handled for you.

languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.thinki.title: Show Effort Variants In Model Picker
languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.thinki.markdownDescription: List each reasoning model once per effort level in the chat model picker, as `Claude Sonnet 4.6 · think high`. Picking one of these sets the effort for that conversation only, overriding `#languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.thinking.effort#`. A `· think off` entry is also listed while `#languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.thinking.enabled#` is on, which is the only way to turn reasoning off for a single conversation. Off by default because it multiplies the number of entries in the picker. The status bar item still sets the default used by the plain entries.

languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.thinki.title: Thinking Budget Tokens (0 = derive from effort)
languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.thinki.markdownDescription: Explicit thinking token budget for models that use the older budget-based reasoning API. **`0` derives it from `#languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.thinking.effort#`**, which is recommended. Values below 1024 are raised to 1024, Anthropic's documented floor. The budget is always kept below `#languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.maxOutputTokens#` so the model still has room to answer, and that limit is raised to fit when it is left at `0`. Ignored by models that choose their own budget.

languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.thinki.title: Show Thinking
enumDescriptions: Use the editor's own thinking display where available, otherwise show nothing.
Always show reasoning, inside a collapsed block above the answer.
languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.thinki.markdownDescription: How to display reasoning output. `native` needs an editor build that can render thinking; on builds that cannot, it shows nothing, so choose `text` to see reasoning everywhere. Reasoning is captured for the model's own use either way.

languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.native.title: Use Bedrock Token Counting
languageModelChatProvider.bedrock.native.markdownDescription: Ask Bedrock to count a request's input tokens with the model's own tokenizer before sending it. Exact rather than estimated, at the cost of one extra API call per turn. Disable to rely on local estimation only.

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run clean && npm run compile
